# Story Candidate Catalog

The 98 developed documentary candidates, in release order. Each entry is a candidate, not a commission.

> **What a catalogue entry is.** A premise supported by named sources for the core situation, with an identified place and an identified kind of activity. **It is not a verified story.** No person has agreed to take part. No filming access exists. Nothing labelled as visual or sound material has been filmed; it is a description of what exists in a place, offered as a proposed opportunity.

> **The philosophical connection in each entry is an interpretation held by the production team.** It is never given to a participant as an explanation of their life, and every entry carries the idea card's own limits as evidence that could contradict it. Where reality contradicts the reading, reality wins and the entry changes.

## E2 - `ST-007` Two skins, two voices

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lead** | `SL-SQ02-001` |
| **Release** | Episode 2, S01, position 1 of 7 |
| **Candidate status** | `evidenced-situation` |
| **Territory / question** | T01 / SQ02 |
| **Primary idea** | `C101-I02` - Hearing the faint by starting with the loud |
| **Supporting ideas** | `C065-I01` Feeling what you reached for, `C073-I03` What a description cannot give you |
| **Concept sources** | `C101` |
| **Continuity role** | primary anchor, rank 1 (object and sound) |
| **Chronology** | phase `P3`, confidence `seasonal` |
| **Production difficulty** | **low** - nothing beyond ordinary location filming |

**Premise.** Published accounts describe drum-making settlements near Kandy, one with about 33 families and over 200 artisans supplying schools, temples and dancers, and another at Kuragandeniya in Menikhinna with about 15 families. The same accounts report shortages of hides and of suitable wood.

**Subject and location.** Drum makers producing geta bera and other traditional drums for temples, schools and Kandyan dancers. Kuragandeniya, Menikhinna, and the drum-making settlements near Kandy (Kandy, Central province).

**Observable activity.** Hollowing a single block of jak, kohomba, ehela or red sandalwood; preparing and mounting two different vellums so that the two heads sound against each other; tensioning; testing by ear.

**Central human question.** How do we learn to hear what is quiet without being overwhelmed by everything else?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Raw-material scarcity, named in the sources as hides and wood, is an ongoing constraint that can be observed rather than asserted.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** The situation is constrained by a season or a work cycle, so there is a window rather than a date.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Hollowing a single block of jak, kohomba, ehela or red sandalwood; preparing and mounting two different vellums so that the two heads sound against each other; tensioning; testing by ear.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** Raw-material scarcity, named in the sources as hides and wood, is an ongoing constraint that can be observed rather than asserted. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (encyclopaedia entry, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): About 33 families and over 200 artisans in one drum-making settlement; about 15 families at Kuragandeniya in Menikhinna; scarcity of deer, goat, rabbit and iguana hides and of suitable wood.  
  <https://globalinch.org/craft/musical-instruments-of-sri-lanka/>
- **S2** (reference, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The geta bera is made from a single block of wood, commonly jak, with two contrasting vellums, and accompanies Kandyan dance.  
  <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geta_bera>
- **S3** (magazine feature, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Descriptive account of the drum-making process.  
  <https://exploresrilanka.lk/the-making-of-the-beraya/>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Whether the hide shortage is a legal supply question, a wildlife-protection question or a price question. The sources name the shortage but not its cause.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. Schools and temples are named as customers, which gives a possible route through a dance school rather than through the workshop.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Animal hides are central to the craft. The subject must be handled factually, without either sensationalising it or concealing it, and the legal position on protected species must be checked before filming.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Hearing the faint by starting with the loud - Fine listening can be built in graded steps. A listener starts with sounds that are already obvious, moves toward quieter and nearer ones, widens the field a little at a time, and settles again before telling one sound from another. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The supernormal hearing is a doctrinal claim and is not supported here. Nothing in the source establishes that this sequence improves ordinary hearing, and it must not be presented as audiology or cognitive science. Skilled listeners may learn through immersion, mentoring or repetition instead of any graded plan. Differences in listening can also reflect hearing ability or experience rather than attention training.

**Premise.** Coir craft is documented in these named Kalutara villages. Sector sources describe coir as a long-established cottage industry, with spinning and weaving employing large numbers regionally, many of them women working part-time, alongside about 10,000 direct and 20,000 indirect jobs in the Sri Lankan coir sector.

**Subject and location.** Coir fibre and rope work in the Kalutara coastal villages. Pohaddaramulla, Waskaduwa, Narampitiyawa, Pothupitiya and Panadura (Kalutara, Western province).

**Observable activity.** Retting, beating and cleaning fibre, spinning yarn, twisting rope, drying yards; the difference between hand work and mill work in the same district.

**Central human question.** What in our surroundings reaches us every day without ever becoming something we notice?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Not established as a current event. The live question is what share of the work is still done by hand and by whom.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Retting, beating and cleaning fibre, spinning yarn, twisting rope, drying yards; the difference between hand work and mill work in the same district.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** Not established as a current event. The live question is what share of the work is still done by hand and by whom. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (encyclopaedia entry, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Coir craft in the Kalutara district in the villages of Pohaddaramulla, Waskaduwa, Narampitiyawa, Pothupitiya and Panadura.  
  <https://www.globalinch.org/craft/mat-weaving-other-rush-ware-fibre-ware-leaf-crafts/>
- **S2** (government sector overview, published 2023-03, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Official sector overview of coir and coir-based products.  
  <https://www.industry.gov.lk/web/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Sector-overview-coir-and-coir-based-products-sector.pdf>
- **S3** (trade body, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Coir has been a major cottage industry for centuries; products include twines, ropes, mats, brushes and geotextiles.  
  <https://www.srilankabusiness.com/coconut/coconut-fibre-products.html>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Whether hand rope-twisting still happens in these villages or has moved entirely to mills. Not established. Employment figures come from mixed regional sources and must not be attributed to one village.

**Research and access route.** No contact made.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Retting work is wet, low-paid and often women's work. It must not be filmed as texture for a sequence about something else.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Not everything that reaches us gets noticed - Things that reach the senses are processed to very different depths. A vivid thing sets off a full response, while a faint one may only stir the mind and leave nothing behind. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The grades and counts are doctrinal, not attention science. The source does not discuss importance or neglect; that is my extension. Noticing also depends on training, expectation, care and emotional state, which this account does not address. Not noticing something is not a moral failure.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-062` The people who work the mountain nobody looks at - Work nobody looks at, in a material everyone uses, and then work nobody looks at that everyone would rather not.

**Premise.** UNESCO inscribed Rukada Natya on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2018, the first Sri Lankan element on that list. The inscription records that it is performed by family groups belonging to or connected with the Gamwari lineage in these towns, that puppeteers make their own puppets and handwritten scripts, and that performances have traditionally been held

**Subject and location.** String-puppet families of the Gamwari lineage performing Rukada Natya. Ambalangoda, Balapitiya and Mirissa (Galle and Matara, Southern province).

**Observable activity.** Carving and stringing puppets; writing and reciting scripts; a small band; a performance where the audience watches the figure and not the hands above it.

**Central human question.** What in a familiar place have we never actually seen?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** An inscribed tradition with a declining number of practising families; the May-June performance season is a real, datable window.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** There is a date: Performances traditionally at temples in May and June.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Carving and stringing puppets; writing and reciting scripts; a small band; a performance where the audience watches the figure and not the hands above it.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** An inscribed tradition with a declining number of practising families; the May-June performance season is a real, datable window. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (UNESCO inscription, published 2018, accessed 2026-09-18, confirmed by fetching the page): Inscribed 2018 on the Representative List (13.COM); performed by family groups of the Gamwari lineage around Ambalangoda, Balapitiya and Mirissa; puppeteers make their own puppets and handwritten scripts; performances traditionally at temples and community centres in May and June; the related nadagam form is described as extinct.  
  <https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/rukada-natya-traditional-string-puppet-drama-in-sri-lanka-01370>
- **S2** (newspaper, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Independent confirmation that this was Sri Lanka's first inscription on the Representative List.  
  <https://www.ft.lk/front-page/R%C5%ABkada-N%C5%ABtya-first-from-Lanka-to-be-on-UNESCO-s-List-of-Intangible-Cultural-Heritage-of-Humanity/44-667885>
- **S3** (news interview, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Reporting that puppetry is not a viable living and that younger people are leaving the form.  
  <https://www.themorning.lk/articles/hFMTOARGjLGZiH1LKFY5>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** How many Gamwari families still perform, and whether any performance is scheduled in the coming May-June window. Not established.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. The UNESCO file names museums as a route, which is a formal and appropriate first approach.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** An inscribed heritage element attracts attention that can distort it. Filming must not become another demand on a small number of families.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Most of what meets the eye goes unseen - Countless sights reach the eyes, but only those the mind turns toward are actually seen. Seeing depends on attention as much as on eyes and light. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's account of eye-sensitivity and the heart-base is traditional physiology and doctrine, not neuroscience, and should not be presented as matching modern findings. Failing to notice something may also come from poor visibility, fatigue, unfamiliarity or simply not knowing what to look for, rather than from where attention was directed. Skilled noticing may reflect trained knowledge more than desire to see.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-006` The looking is what wears it away - ST-001 is about attention deliberately steered away from a mechanism: an audience watching a puppet and not the hand. ST-006 is about attention so concentrated on one object that the concentration damages it. One is a craft depending on not being seen; the other is a site being worn by being seen.

**Premise.** Laksha work applies resin from the lac insect to turned wood. In the niyapoten veda technique the lac is drawn out and severed with the thumbnail, and the finished piece is polished with a talipot leaf and coconut oil. Published accounts name Hapuwida in Matale as a village with a handful of remaining artisans, and at least one press piece is titled as being about Sri Lanka's last lacquer workers.

**Subject and location.** Lacquer (laksha) workers using the niyapoten veda fingernail technique. Hapuwida in Matale; Angulmaduwa near Tangalle; Hurikaduwa near Kandy; Pallekanda near Balangoda (Matale, Hambantota, Kandy, Ratnapura, Central, Southern, Sabaragamuwa province).

**Observable activity.** Breeding and collecting the lac resin, washing, drying and filtering it; heating; laying colour on a turning piece; severing with the thumbnail; polishing.

**Central human question.** When we reach out already knowing what we want to feel, what do our hands stop telling us?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** A named technique with a named village and a small, countable number of practitioners.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Breeding and collecting the lac resin, washing, drying and filtering it; heating; laying colour on a turning piece; severing with the thumbnail; polishing.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** A named technique with a named village and a small, countable number of practitioners. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (newspaper, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Press treatment of the remaining lacquer workers; to be read in full before any number is used.  
  <https://www.thesun.lk/front_page/AnchorSri-Lankas-Last-Lacquer-Workers/557-304461l>
- **S2** (craft body, published 2021-06-01, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The lac resin is secreted by an insect, bred on suitable trees, then scraped, washed, dried and filtered; the niyapoten veda technique uses the fingernail, and the piece is polished with a talipot leaf coated in coconut oil.  
  <https://ceylonhandicraft.lk/2021/06/01/traditional-laksha-industry-in-srilanka/>
- **S3** (craft documentation, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Names Matale-Hapuvida, Tangalle-Angulmaduwa, Kandy-Hurikaduwa and Balangoda-Pallekanda as the main laksha centres.  
  <https://www.hidmc.com/blog-posts/documenting-sri-lankas-traditional-crafts-and-artisans>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** How many artisans at Hapuwida still work niyapoten veda rather than brush or spray finishing. Not established.

**Research and access route.** No contact made.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** The 'last practitioner' framing is used by several of these sources. It must be checked rather than adopted, because it is a framing that sells.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Feeling what you reached for - When we touch something, several qualities meet the skin at once, but we register only one. Which one depends on what we were expecting and on our own body, which is the measure against which hot and cold are felt. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This comes from a doctrinal analysis of matter, not experiment, and must not be presented as neuroscience. Missing a quality may come from fatigue, numbness, haste or lack of training rather than expectation. The selective role of wanting in sight is already carded in C009-I01. This card's distinct points are touch and the body as its own baseline.

**Similar candidates.** None in the catalogue shares this candidate's primary idea or question.

Flat-bottome

**Subject and location.** People using and maintaining the Hamilton canal and the older Dutch canal system. The canal from the Kelani river to Negombo, through the Muthurajawela wetland (Colombo, Gampaha, Western province).

**Observable activity.** A boat moving at walking pace beside a main road, fishing in the canal, and the wetland it drains.

**Central human question.** What do we miss experiencing when we are busy getting through it?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Not a current event. The material is a 200-year-old piece of infrastructure still in use for something other than what it was built for.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

  <https://exploresrilanka.lk/the-hamilton-canal-a-past-and-future-waterway/>

**How the philosophical reading works.** When hurry leaves nothing fully taken in - An agitated mind, pulled by sudden demands or many tasks at once, may be unable to stay with anything long enough to take it in, so that even good or bad things register flatly. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source describes a doctrinal momentary mind-state, not a finding about multitasking or stress. It should not be equated with neuroscience. Flat feeling during busy periods may instead come from fatigue, practised routine, or a deliberate focus on the task. Some people report feeling most alive when busy. Memory of an event is not a reliable measure of how fully it was experienced.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Knowing the sign without knowing the reason - We recognise things by marks that repetition has laid down. That recognition can become firm and quick without ever including an understanding of what the thing is or why it is so. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source analyses a mental factor within a doctrinal framework. It is not a cognitive science account of memory or pattern recognition and should not be equated with one. Long familiarity often does carry real practical knowledge that the source's simple example does not capture. An alternative reading is that a person who “only recognises” may understand a great deal but lack words or formal explanation for it.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

ST-017 is a bite that has to be identified in minutes, usually without the animal. Same mechanism, opposite timescales, and in the second case the not-knowing is measurably lethal.

**How the philosophical reading works.** When a passing quality becomes a person's name - Words such as "the greedy one" or "the wise one" take a quality that really occurs and fasten it to a person as a lasting name. It treats these names as valid conventions, and many labels are accurate, affectionate or useful. A stable trait may genuinely justify a lasting description, and people sometimes embrace their labels. The source's list includes a colour-based example ("the white man"); this card does not extend to race or appearance.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-091` Whose forest the field is - Cultivators prosecuted for clearing forest, and a community whose hunting was made an offence by the same kind of instrument.

Reactions can be shaped by trauma, fatigue, illness or coercion, so a response need not reflect free choice. Outsiders cannot see where impression ended and response began.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Knowing the cost and still wanting it - Knowing that an action has consequences does not necessarily remove the desire to do it. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This is a limited application of one doctrinal distinction, not a translation of the full eightfold classification. The source's explanation involves habit across lifetimes, which is a doctrinal claim. An outwardly similar choice may come from necessity, social pressure, obligation or a lack of real alternatives rather than unrestrained desire. Behaviour alone cannot show that a person “knows the cost”. Only their own account, handled carefully, could suggest it.

**Ethical concerns.** High. A person awaiting trial is presumed innocent and identifying them can do lasting harm. Remand prisoners are in custody and cannot freely consent. Nothing may be filmed that prejudices a live case.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Restless yet still gripping the same thing - A mind can be agitated and unsettled while still holding on to one object. Being restless does not mean being free of what one is fixed on. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source describes a momentary unwholesome mind-state in a doctrinal classification, not rumination, anxiety or any clinical condition. It must not be used to diagnose anyone or to suggest that worry is morally wrong. Returning again and again to a problem can also be necessary problem-solving, protective vigilance or grief, rather than agitation.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-020` The thing that waits - A dormant pull waiting for its trigger, and a case waiting seventeen years for a hearing.
- `ST-094` The person who opens the sluice - A village that hands one person the power to decide, against a national system in which a million cases wait for a decision.

**Merge note.** A separate lead on prison overcrowding was opened and then merged into this one. The two are the same situation seen from its two ends: the pending case and the person waiting for it. Keeping them apart would have produced two episodes with the same cause, the same figures and the same institutional sources.

**Central human question.** When we need to be pushed, is it the will that is missing, or the strength and practice?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** A documented generational gap in an occupation whose daily physical demand is visible in the work itself.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Climbing before dawn, cutting and binding the inflorescence, collecting and lowering pots, the walk between trees, delivery to a co-operative.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** A documented generational gap in an occupation whose daily physical demand is visible in the work itself. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (news agency, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Younger generations unwilling to take on the risk; numbers dwindling for decades; falls in rain and wind; adulterated toddy from imported synthetic materials.  
  <https://globalpressjournal.com/asia/sri_lanka/toddy-tapping-traditional-sri-lankan-job-faces-extinction/index.html>
- **S2** (newspaper, published 2021-12-28, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): About 10,000 people in Jaffna engaged in growing and tapping palmyrah and about 800 working as helpers; co-operatives capping purchases; low profit from sap.  
  <https://archives1.dailynews.lk/2021/12/28/business/268587/top-toddy-sri-lanka%E2%80%99s-tree-tapping-trade-reaches-new-heights>
- **S3** (documentary photography, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Existing photographic documentation of the work, useful for checking what has already been covered.  
  <https://www.antoinejonquiere.com/toddy-tappers>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Current tapper numbers and ages. The 10,000 figure is from 2021 and covers growing as well as tapping.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. The palmyrah co-operatives and the Palmyrah Development Board are institutional routes.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** This is alcohol production with a licensing regime and a public-health dimension, and the work involves real fall risk. Nobody should climb for the camera, and no climb should be repeated for a better angle.

**How the philosophical reading works.** When a tired body makes every act need pushing - Whether an action arises readily or needs urging depends partly on the condition of body and mind and on practised skill. Ease and skill go with readiness; exhaustion and heaviness go with needing a push. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source states these conditions briefly and does not claim they are the only causes. Alternative explanations for needing a push include fear, doubt, conflicting duties, lack of interest, illness or coercion. Seeing that someone needed urging does not show whether they were tired, unskilled or unwilling.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-029` Three in the morning, every morning - ST-026 is about the daily climb of a palmyrah tapper in the north, where the sources record the physical risk driving young people away. ST-029 is about a rubber tapper's pre-dawn start in the south-west, where the sources record wages and status driving them away. The body is the site in both, but the pressure on it is different and so is the region and the crop.

  <https://www.1990.lk/about-us/>

Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** High. A patient in an emergency cannot give meaningful consent at the time. Nothing filmed during a call may be used without consent obtained afterwards, from the patient or, if they died, from the family, and the default must be that it is not used.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Having a skill but not reaching it in time - Doing something with time to prepare differs from doing it at once when a threat arrives. Using that speed to protect others is rarer still. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The feats are doctrinal powers and are not claimed here; only the graded structure is used, as analogy. Speed under pressure may depend on temperament, rehearsal of specific scenarios, fitness, equipment or teamwork rather than depth of mastery. Freezing in an emergency can be a normal stress response, not a lack of skill, and must not be read as failure of character.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-034` Not enough hands for the bark - ST-034 is a national shortage of a skill with a harvest window measured in weeks. ST-035 is an individual skill with a window measured in minutes. The scale and the clock are different, and so is who bears the cost of being late.

Some people react to such knowledge with resentment or paralysis rather than resolve.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Knowing when to push and when to leave alone - Steady work on something difficult may need three different moves at different times: pushing, cooling down and simply watching. **Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source describes a meditator balancing mental factors toward liberation, not a general theory of work or care. The goldsmith and charioteer are its similes; craft practice is my extension. Knowing when to intervene may rest on tacit skill, external signals, instructions or luck rather than any inner balancing. Hesitating to intervene can also be avoidance rather than wise restraint.

**Premise.** Beeralu is a bobbin-lace technique introduced in the colonial period and worked mainly by women along the southern coast. Published accounts describe it as slowly disappearing because the work is long and arduous, alongside recent revival efforts including state promotion and use by fashion labels.

**Subject and location.** Women lace-makers working beeralu (bobbin lace) in the southern coastal villages. Galle, Magalle, Makuluwa, Weligama, Mirissa, Gandara, Dikwella, Kottegoda (Galle and Matara, Southern province).

**Observable activity.** Working a pillow of bobbins by hand at a household pace; pattern cards; selling at the fort; teaching demonstrations for visitors.

**Central human question.** How do we decide to trust an account of something we have never experienced?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** A craft being kept alive partly by demand from outside the community it belongs to. What that does to the work, and to what the maker is paid, is researchable.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Working a pillow of bobbins by hand at a household pace; pattern cards; selling at the fort; teaching demonstrations for visitors.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** A craft being kept alive partly by demand from outside the community it belongs to. What that does to the work, and to what the maker is paid, is researchable. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (news feature, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Beeralu is practised by women in Galle, Matara, Makuluwa, Gandara, Dikwella, Kottegoda, Mirissa, Magalle and Weligama; the craft is described as on the verge of being forgotten.  
  <https://archive.roar.media/english/life/culture-identities/art-of-lace-beeralu-kept-alive>
- **S2** (trade body blog, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The term renda is Portuguese and beeralu derives from Portuguese; state initiatives promote the craft as a source of income for artisan women in coastal villages.  
  <https://www.srilankabusiness.com/blog/dutch-lace-making.html>
- **S3** (newspaper, published 2015-06-28, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Independent newspaper account of the technique and its practitioners.  
  <https://www.sundaytimes.lk/150628/funday-times/crafting-beeralu-lace-154464.html>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** How many women still work beeralu commercially, and what a piece earns against the hours it takes. No reliable current figure was found.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. Demonstration sessions for visitors exist at Galle Fort, which is a route in but is not the same as filming a working household.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Low-paid women's home work. Earnings must not be reported from a seller's figure, and no maker should be filmed in a way that implies she is content with the rate.

**How the philosophical reading works.** What a description cannot give you - Some things cannot be understood from another person's description. Without direct experience we rely on inference and trust, and even a little first-hand experience changes what a description can convey. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's claim that nibbāna is reached only by supramundane insight is doctrinal and not endorsed here. Its blindness illustration must not become a metaphor for ignorance; people blind from birth have full understanding of their own. Much does transfer well through language and teaching, and failed learning may reflect poor teaching rather than a limit of description.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-039` Before you are allowed to write - ST-038 is a skill that lives in the hands and cannot be conveyed in words. ST-039 is a skill gated by permission, where a long apprenticeship precedes being allowed to begin at all. Inarticulable technique and controlled access are different problems.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This is a limited analogy. Alternative explanations: fluent performers may still silently use the words without noticing, and dropping the words may reflect automatic habit rather than deeper understanding.

The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source concerns meditative absorptions and a doctrinal path. It says nothing about crafts or sport. Insistence on mastery may also reflect tradition or safety rules. Quick entry under pressure is a separate question, covered by C089-I01.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. Zonal education offices and principals are the route, and ministry approval is needed.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Very high. The subjects include children who cannot consent for themselves. A school must not be identified as failing, and no child should be shown in a way that marks them as coming from a poor school.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Fitting an explanation to where someone is confused - The same understanding can be taught in different shapes. Which helps depends on what a learner is confused about, and whether they need it short or detailed. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source concerns the Buddha's teaching and a doctrinal analysis of experience; carrying it into ordinary teaching is interpretation. Its ranking of people by "sharp" and "dull" faculties must not be applied to real learners. Learners may not know where they are confused, a preference for brevity may reflect time rather than need, and tailoring can leave some people with a thinner version.

**How the philosophical reading works.** A hard road does not mean slow understanding - How hard it is to keep practising something and how quickly understanding comes are two separate things. A person can struggle and still understand fast, or find the work easy and still understand slowly. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Premise.** Sector studies and press reporting describe a shortage of roughly 35,000 peelers, with the consequence that only about 35 per cent of the crop is harvested twice a year while about 65 per cent is harvested once. Reported figures put cinnamon at about 35,000 hectares with about 60,000 growers and about 300,000 workers, and the livelihood reaching roughly 350,000 families. A Cinnamon Training Academ

**Subject and location.** Cinnamon peelers and the households and training academies trying to replace them. Cinnamon-growing areas of the southern and south-western coast and interior (Galle, Matara, Hambantota, Ratnapura, Kalutara and Uva areas, Southern, Sabaragamuwa, Uva, Western province).

**Observable activity.** Cutting, rubbing, slitting and peeling the bark; rolling quills; drying sheds; the training benches where new peelers learn on real sticks.

**Central human question.** What turns something we know how to do into something we can do the moment someone needs it?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** A skill with a time window: the bark peels properly only within a period, and the reported consequence of too few peelers is a halved harvest cycle. That is a measurable, currently live situation.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** There is a date: Peeling follows the harvest cycle.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Cutting, rubbing, slitting and peeling the bark; rolling quills; drying sheds; the training benches where new peelers learn on real sticks.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** A skill with a time window: the bark peels properly only within a period, and the reported consequence of too few peelers is a halved harvest cycle. That is a measurable, currently live situation. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (donor-funded sector study, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Shortage of about 35,000 peelers; non-recognition of skilled capability; workers migrating to non-agricultural work; about 35 per cent of the crop harvested twice a year and about 65 per cent once.  
  <https://standardsfacility.org/sites/default/files/PG_343_Study_Master_Plan_Final.pdf>
- **S2** (business press, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): About 35,000 hectares, about 60,000 farmers and about 300,000 workers; training by the Cinnamon Training Academy under its chairman Sarada De Silva; social stigma attached to peeling.  
  <https://www.ft.lk/Agriculture/labour-shortage-hits-cinnamon-industry/31-624902>
- **S3** (government research institute, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Official research on the industry including payment systems, where peelers are paid by a share of the harvest and the share differs by area.  
  <https://www.harti.gov.lk/images/download/reasearch_report/report_203.pdf>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Current (2026) peeler numbers and wage rates. The figures above come from different years and must not be presented as a single current picture.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. The training academy is an institution and is a realistic first approach; individual peeling households are not.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Low pay and occupational stigma are documented. The stigma is a fact about how the work is regarded; it must never be restated as a judgement about peelers, and no peeler should be asked on camera to comment on their own social standing without preparation and a right to withdraw.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Having a skill but not reaching it in time - Doing something with time to prepare differs from doing it at once when a threat arrives. Using that speed to protect others is rarer still. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The feats are doctrinal powers and are not claimed here; only the graded structure is used, as analogy. Speed under pressure may depend on temperament, rehearsal of specific scenarios, fitness, equipment or teamwork rather than depth of mastery. Freezing in an emergency can be a normal stress response, not a lack of skill, and must not be read as failure of character.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-035` Fifteen minutes and thirty-two seconds - ST-034 is a national shortage of a skill with a harvest window measured in weeks. ST-035 is an individual skill with a window measured in minutes. The scale and the clock are different, and so is who bears the cost of being late.

**Subject and location.** The Jaffna Public Library, its present users and staff, and what was lost in 1981. Jaffna Public Library (Jaffna, Northern province).

**Observable activity.** The reading rooms as they are used now, the catalogue, and whatever remains of the pre-1981 holdings.

**Central human question.** After something important has changed, how do we tell what is truly behind us from what is still with us?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Not a current event. The live question is what a restored institution can and cannot restore, and that is answerable by looking at the shelves.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* The reading rooms as they are used now, the catalogue, and whatever remains of the pre-1981 holdings.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** Not a current event. The live question is what a restored institution can and cannot restore, and that is answerable by looking at the shelves. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (reference, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The date of 31 May 1981; the reported 97,000 volumes and manuscripts; the restoration programme, its reported cost and funding, the 1984 partial reopening and the 2003 full reopening; the permanence of the loss.  
  <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_of_the_Jaffna_Public_Library>
- **S2** (news agency, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Independent reporting on the library's destruction and rebuilding.  
  <https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/burnt-rebuilt-jaffna-library-reminds-of-sri-lanka-conflict/153795>
- **S3** (academic institute, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Scholarly teaching resource on the event and its historiography.  
  <https://www.aisls.org/teaching-about-the-sri-lankan-civil-war/1981-burning-of-the-jaffna-public-library/>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** How many pre-1981 items survive, and whether any are catalogued as such. Attribution of responsibility for the burning is contested in the sources and must be reported as attributed, not asserted.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. The library is run by the Jaffna Municipal Council.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** High. The event is part of a contested national history and any account of it will be read politically. The film should keep to what the library can show and to what the people who use it now say, rather than narrating the conflict over them.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Taking stock of what is gone and what remains - After a real turning point, it is possible to look back in separate ways: at what was achieved, at what it brought, at what has truly been left behind, and at what is still there. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). In the source, the reviewing follows a doctrinal event in which mental stains are cut off permanently. Everyday change is gradual and reversible. People may skip stock-taking out of exhaustion, humility, cultural reticence or because the change is still fragile, not out of complacency. Self-assessment can also be distorted by optimism or harsh self-criticism.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-037` The last hana weavers of Henawala - ST-037 is a craft counting how many households still practise it. ST-078 is an institution counting what survived a destruction. One is attrition; the other is a single night.

Dansal and pandals are also competitive and sponsored, and a supporting idea in this lead is about giving turning into outdoing others. **That is a possible reading, not a finding**, and it must not be imposed on volunteers who may simply be feeding people. If the evidence points the other way, the film says so.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Feeding others for the joy of watching them - An act that looks like kindness, such as feeding an animal or a small child, can come from wanting to help or from the pleasure of watching. **Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's categories do not say that enjoying an animal's company is harmful. Pleasure and genuine care often coexist. Whether feeding actually helps an animal is a separate factual and ecological question the source does not address. Feeding wildlife can also cause harm. Do not portray people who keep or feed animals as selfish on the basis of observation alone.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Giving away only what you would not keep - Two gifts of the same size can differ sharply. **Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This is a doctrinal classification of donors, not a rule that people should deprive themselves. Differences in what is given can reflect custom, health needs or what the receiver prefers rather than the giver's attitude.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Goodness that ends once its reward arrives - Good conduct kept as a means to something else has a built-in end point. **Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source ranks conduct by motive for doctrinal ends, including rebirth. Its praise of keeping precepts even at the cost of life must not be carried forward. Conduct that relaxes after a goal may reflect a deliberate, time-bound commitment, exhaustion or changed circumstances rather than a hidden bargain. Mixed motives are normal, and outsiders cannot see which one held a person's conduct in place.

**Subject and location.** Leopards dying in snares in the central highlands, and the people who live and work in that landscape. Tea estate mosaics and forest patches of the central highlands (Nuwara Eliya and neighbouring hill districts, Central and Uva province).

**Stakes and uncertainty.** A recently published study with a clear and unwelcome finding, and conservation practice that has not yet caught up with it.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Holding back from harm, with or without a promise - People stop themselves from harm in at least two ways: by responding to the moment when the chance arrives, or by holding to an earlier commitment even at a cost. **Ethical concerns.** Very high. This involves alleged organised illegality with alleged political protection. Filming at night at an active site would put a crew and any local guide at real risk, and anyone who speaks on camera could face retaliation. This lead may only proceed through established community organisations, with a security assessment, and possibly without identifying anyone.

**How the philosophical reading works.** How one crossed line makes the next easier - Once a person has done serious harm, restraint elsewhere can loosen too. A wrong already done becomes a strong support for further wrongs, of the same kind and of other kinds. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's illustrations include killing a parent and splitting the monastic community, with fixed rebirth results. These are doctrinal and not carried over. Escalation may instead come from opportunity, peer pressure, debt, addiction, coercion, or the need to cover up the first act. Many people stop after one wrong. No documentary subject should be framed as on a slope toward harm.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-056` What happens underground when nobody is watching - A miner alone underground with a stone, against a riverbed mined at night under a court order that is not enforced.
- `ST-057` What the seniors do because the seniors did it - ST-055 is an illegal extraction continuing for two decades after a court banned it. ST-057 is a practice inside an institution that renews itself each academic year. Both are escalation, one across time and one across cohorts.

**Ethical concerns.** The story touches on alleged corruption. Filming people who depend on permits, while that allegation is in the air, could expose them. Anonymity options must be settled before any approach.

**How the philosophical reading works.** When stockpiling turns shared plenty into boundaries - When people move from taking what they need to storing up, something held in common can start to seem scarce. It gets divided, and division makes it possible to take what is someone else's. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source presents a myth, with magical elements, as cosmic history. It does not show that stockpiling causes theft. Division of common resources often follows population growth, state policy or real scarcity rather than changed habits. Boundaries can also reduce conflict, and storing food is often a sensible answer to uncertainty.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Sorting and carrying, the weighing and sale of recovered material, the site itself, and the new plants going up alongside it.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** A documented transition to formal waste processing that is displacing an existing informal livelihood. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (environmental news, published 2026-04, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Current state of open dumping and reform failure; marginalisation of informal collectors; the informal recycling sector sidelined by new plants.  
  <https://news.mongabay.com/2026/04/open-dumping-failed-reforms-bury-sri-lankan-cities-in-waste-problem/>
- **S2** (environmental NGO, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The 25-acre wetland site at Boralesgamuwa-Borupana adjacent to the Weras Ganga flowing into Bolgoda Lake; the 2019 National Building Research Organisation warning of possible collapse.  
  <https://efl.lk/karadiyana-garbage-dump/>
- **S3** (environmental NGO, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The 2017 Meethotamulla collapse: 32 killed, more than 140 homes destroyed, hundreds displaced.  
  <https://efl.lk/status-waste-management-sri-lanka/>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** How many people currently make a living at Karadiyana, and whether any transition support exists for them. Not established.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. The site is operated by a local authority; the people who work it are not employed by it, which makes consent a question for them, not for the authority.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Very high. Stigma is documented, and a film can deepen it. Nobody should be filmed in a way that makes their work look degrading, children must not be filmed at the site at all, and the 2017 deaths are within living memory for the same neighbourhoods.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Suffering nobody sees unless they ask - Some suffering is visible, and its cause is plain. Other suffering, such as bodily aches or inner turmoil, can only be known if someone asks, and its cause is not evident. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's list is a doctrinal analysis within a teaching that all conditioned feeling is suffering. It is not a medical or psychological classification. It does not say that hidden suffering is worse. People may conceal pain by choice, from dignity, stoicism or fear of being a burden, so not asking can sometimes respect privacy. Asking can also intrude. Visible harm can go unacknowledged too.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-002` What the rope is made of - Work nobody looks at, in a material everyone uses, and then work nobody looks at that everyone would rather not.
- `ST-064` Two hundred kilometres for a prescription - ST-062 concerns work that is in plain sight and looked away from. ST-064 concerns distress that is not in sight at all and that the service system is not positioned to find. The first is avoidance; the second is absence.

Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**How the philosophical reading works.** When stockpiling turns shared plenty into boundaries - When people move from taking what they need to storing up, something held in common can start to seem scarce. It gets divided, and division makes it possible to take what is someone else's. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source presents a myth, with magical elements, as cosmic history. It does not show that stockpiling causes theft. Division of common resources often follows population growth, state policy or real scarcity rather than changed habits. Boundaries can also reduce conflict, and storing food is often a sensible answer to uncertainty.

**Ethical concerns.** Moderate to high. Compensation claims are live; nothing filmed should weaken a claim. Fishers have been interviewed repeatedly since 2021 and may reasonably be tired of it.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Trying to outweigh past harm with later good - People try to balance earlier harm with later good. That effort can change the weight of the past, but it may not erase it. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

**Premise.** Published figures record around 3,000 suicides a year in Sri Lanka, roughly eight to nine a day, with a 2022 rate of about 15 per 100,000 overall and a large gap between men and women, and record that around 70 per cent of cases are rural. Research records that psychotropic medication is not available in rural clinics, requiring patients to travel 50 to 100 km to renew a prescription, and identifi

**Subject and location.** Rural mental health services, community counsellors and the people they are meant to reach. Rural districts (multiple, multiple province).

**Observable activity.** A clinic day, the journey to reach it, a counsellor's round, and the helpline.

**Central human question.** What suffering around us goes unknown simply because no one thinks to ask?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Live capacity-building work against a measured and persistent problem.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* A clinic day, the journey to reach it, a counsellor's round, and the helpline.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** Live capacity-building work against a measured and persistent problem. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (university policy unit, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Research-based policy briefing on suicide prevention in Sri Lanka.  
  <https://www.bristol.ac.uk/policybristol/policy-briefings/preventing-suicide-sri-lanka/>
- **S2** (peer-reviewed journal, published 2024, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The rural service gap including unavailability of psychotropic medication in rural clinics and the travel required; the populations identified as vulnerable.  
  <https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666560324000926>
- **S3** (UN agency, published 2025-09-10, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): WHO support for counsellor training and the district-level helpline, and the current framing of the problem.  
  <https://www.who.int/srilanka/news/detail/10-09-2025-world-suicide-prevention-day-2025--changing-the-narrative-on-suicide-in-sri-lanka>
- **S4** (clinical review, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Assessment of underfunding, stigma and service gaps.  
  <https://c4rnhk.org/critical-review-sri-lankas-mental-health-crisis-underfunding-stigma-and-service-gaps/>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Current national figures. The rate cited is from 2022 and has not been updated here.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. The Ministry of Health and the National Institute of Mental Health control clinical access.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** **The highest in this catalogue.** Suicide reporting is governed by established media guidelines on method, location and framing, and those guidelines apply to a documentary. No person in crisis may be filmed. No patient may be filmed in a clinical setting without their own consent taken when they are able to give it. A clinical adviser and a safeguarding protocol are required before any approach, and the project must be prepared to abandon the episode rather than compromise on this.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Suffering nobody sees unless they ask - Some suffering is visible, and its cause is plain. Other suffering, such as bodily aches or inner turmoil, can only be known if someone asks, and its cause is not evident. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's list is a doctrinal analysis within a teaching that all conditioned feeling is suffering. It is not a medical or psychological classification. It does not say that hidden suffering is worse. People may conceal pain by choice, from dignity, stoicism or fear of being a burden, so not asking can sometimes respect privacy. Asking can also intrude. Visible harm can go unacknowledged too.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-062` The people who work the mountain nobody looks at - ST-062 concerns work that is in plain sight and looked away from. ST-064 concerns distress that is not in sight at all and that the service system is not positioned to find. The first is avoidance; the second is absence.

  <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanatte_Cemetery>

  <https://www.sundaytimes.lk/130929/plus/who-goes-there-63818.html>

  <https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/borella-kanatte-general-cemetery>

Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** High. Funerals in progress must not be filmed, and mourners must not appear in the background of a story about the workers. The workers' own dignity is the point, not the morbidity of the setting.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Measuring your own death against the mighty - Many people accept that others die yet feel exempt themselves. Remembering that the most powerful, rich, strong and wise also died can bring the fact home. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The listed figures include legendary, canonical and supernatural beings. The source uses them doctrinally, not as historical evidence. The claim that comparison "settles" the mind is the text's claim. Such reflection might instead produce anxiety, fatalism or cynicism about effort. Unequal access to healthcare means wealth does in fact change when and how people die, which the source's levelling image does not address.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-066` Sixteen beds and the last few weeks - A place where everyone ends up, against a place organised entirely around a known ending.

**Ethical concerns.** High. This story must be made with the community, not about it. Interpretation must be provided for the participants at every stage including consent, and the film must not be built to make hearing viewers feel moved by other people's difficulty.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Hearing the words without the act of meaning - Speaking to someone is a brief act of meaning carried on sound. **Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This is a limited analogy. The source's aim is ultimate analysis for liberation, not a theory of community or grief. Its claim that conventional things “do not truly exist” is doctrinal, and the analysis must not be presented as physics. Many philosophical traditions treat wholes as real in their own right. People's sense that a place or relationship is more than its parts is a legitimate view, not an error to correct.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-074` Five generations at the same mask bench - A workshop in its fifth generation that looks unchanged, against a casting method in which the original must be destroyed to make the object.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Whether any institution holds a catalogued Arwi collection, and whether anyone currently reads Arwi as a working skill. Both are unknown, and the second one decides whether there is a film here.

**Research and access route.** No contact made.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** Kattankudy has a difficult recent history in national coverage. The film must not arrive there via that history, and the community's own priorities should shape whether this is worth doing at all.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Recalling someone's goodness in words you understand - Calling to mind the real qualities of someone deeply respected can lift and steady the mind, but only when the person grasps what they are recalling. Repeating words of praise one does not understand does not do the same work. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). The source's object is the Buddha, whose listed qualities include doctrinal claims such as omniscience; extending the practice to other people is interpretation. The described freedom from craving and anger is doctrinal, not measured. Recited formulas may carry real meaning through rhythm and community without word-by-word understanding. Gladness in remembrance may come from nostalgia or belonging instead. Admiration can also idealise a person.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-087` Words the grandchildren can say but not use - ST-082 is a written script whose readers have gone. ST-087 is a spoken language whose younger speakers can produce the words without using them. Writing and speech, and in the second case the speakers are present.

**Central human question.** What changes when we remember a person's goodness in our own words rather than in the words we were given?

**Premise.** Sri Lanka Railways publishes a disaster recovery and restoration status page, with a version dated 29 December 2025, indicating that restoration work following the December 2025 floods was being tracked at that date. The hill line includes the Demodara loop, where the line passes through a tunnel beneath its own station, and Demodara station is 292.3 km from Colombo. Reporting elsewhere records th

**Subject and location.** Permanent-way and restoration work on the hill-country line, including after the December 2025 floods. The Main Line to Badulla, including the Demodara loop (Nuwara Eliya and Badulla, Central and Uva province).

**Observable activity.** Track and bund repair, slips and clearance, the loop and tunnel, and the trains running through a worksite.

**Central human question.** If everything in something has been replaced bit by bit, what is it that we still feel is the same?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Restoration after a dated disaster, with an official status record.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** There is a date: Restoration work follows the damage.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* Track and bund repair, slips and clearance, the loop and tunnel, and the trains running through a worksite.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** Restoration after a dated disaster, with an official status record. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (state operator, published 2025-12-29, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Official record that disaster recovery and restoration was being tracked as at 29 December 2025.  
  <https://www.railway.gov.lk/web/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=917&Itemid=217&lang=en>
- **S2** (reference, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Demodara is 292.3 km from Colombo; the loop where the line runs through a tunnel beneath the station.  
  <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demodara_railway_station>
- **S3** (heritage site, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Description of the loop's engineering.  
  <https://amazinglanka.com/wp/demodara-loop/>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** What was actually damaged in December 2025 and what remains unrestored. The status page must be read in full, and its current version checked, before anything is claimed.

**Research and access route.** No contact made. Sri Lanka Railways is the permission-holder and trackside filming needs a safety arrangement.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** The December 2025 floods caused deaths and displacement. Railway restoration must not be told as an engineering story that steps over that.

**How the philosophical reading works.** When steady replacement looks like staying the same - Something can seem unchanged for years because its parts are replaced a few at a time, in the same places, so that the change never shows. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This is a limited analogy. The source aims to make a doctrinal claim about momentary matter believable; it is not physics or biology. Things may also seem unchanged because some parts genuinely persist, because people's memories adjust with the change, or because identity is carried by purpose, name or community rather than material. The source does not address meaning or loss; that is my extension.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-074` Five generations at the same mask bench - ST-074 is a workshop whose people are replaced generation by generation. ST-077 is a railway whose physical components are replaced continuously. ST-080 is a product whose name survives a change of substance. Person, material and name: three different things being replaced under one appearance.
- `ST-080` Named after a tree it is mostly no longer made from - ST-074 is a workshop whose people are replaced generation by generation. ST-077 is a railway whose physical components are replaced continuously. ST-080 is a product whose name survives a change of substance. Person, material and name: three different things being replaced under one appearance.
- `ST-084` A line put back where it was - A railway that stays the same by being continuously replaced, against a railway destroyed and rebuilt on its own formation.

**Premise.** The northern railway between Omanthai and Kankesanthurai and between Medawachchiya and Talaimannar Pier was destroyed during the war. Reconstruction of the 265 km northern line was carried out with a line of credit from the Government of India and executed by an Indian state-owned contractor. The Jaffna to Kankesanthurai section reopened on 2 January 2015 after the station had not functioned betwe

**Subject and location.** The reconstructed Northern railway line and the people who use and maintain it. Omanthai to Kankesanthurai and Medawachchiya to Talaimannar Pier (Vavuniya, Kilinochchi, Jaffna, Mannar, Northern province).

**Observable activity.** The working line today, the stations rebuilt on old sites, the Talaimannar Pier terminus, and the ordinary journeys people now make on it.

**Central human question.** What in our past are we still holding on to in order to stand where we are now?

**Stakes and uncertainty.** Not a current event. The change is complete, which makes this a story about what a restored thing carries rather than about a restoration in progress.

**Why filming would be meaningful now.** No calendar forces this. What makes it current is the change described above, and if that change is not real the episode should not be made.

**Proposed visual and sound material.** *Nothing below has been filmed or is known to exist as footage.* The working line today, the stations rebuilt on old sites, the Talaimannar Pier terminus, and the ordinary journeys people now make on it.

**Possible change, with no ending prescribed.** Not a current event. The change is complete, which makes this a story about what a restored thing carries rather than about a restoration in progress. The episode does not know how this resolves and must not be cut as though it did.

**Evidence.**

- **S1** (reference, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Destruction of the Omanthai to Kankesanthurai and Medawachchiya to Talaimannar Pier sections during the war, and the reconstruction project.  
  <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_line_(Sri_Lanka)>
- **S2** (reference, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): The station did not function between 1990 and 2015; the line reopened on 2 January 2015.  
  <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankesanthurai_railway_station>
- **S3** (newspaper, published 2015-03, accessed 2026-09-18, seen in a search result and not yet opened in full): Opening of the Madhu Road to Talaimannar Pier section in March 2015; the 63 km final segment of the 265 km project; Indian line of credit and contractor.  
  <https://www.ft.lk/News/indian-pm-modi-to-inaugurate-rail-track-to-talai-mannar/56-395906>

**Unresolved claims and gaps.** Whether anyone now working the line also worked it before 1990. That single question would turn a piece of infrastructure into a person, and it has not been answered.

**Consent and access status.** No contact has been made. No participant has been approached, no consent of any kind exists, and there is no filming access. Factual verification, whether the situation is still current, participant willingness, filming access and production feasibility are five separate questions and only the first two have been touched here.

**Ethical concerns.** This route runs through places where a great deal happened. It must not be used as a scenic corridor past other people's losses, and the war should not be narrated over the window.

**How the philosophical reading works.** Moving beyond something while still hanging from it - A step that goes beyond an earlier stage can still depend on that stage for its footing. Surpassing something and being free of it are not the same. The reading is applied to the situation, not to any person's character or motive.

**Evidence that could challenge that reading** (from the idea card's own limits). This is a limited analogy. The desert means saṃsāra and the pavilion the formless worlds; these are doctrinal. The dependence in the source is about which mental state serves as object, not about social or historical influence. Many changes do become independent of their origins, and continuity may be chosen rather than hidden.

**Similar candidates, and how they differ.**

- `ST-077` A railway that stays the same by being replaced - A railway that stays the same by being continuously replaced, against a railway destroyed and rebuilt on its own formation.
